subject: blue runner fish
title: A Fish Hides Under Sharks to Ambush Prey, Spotted Just 10% of the Time

scenes.text: The deadliest thing near this shark isn't the shark.
Off a tiny Italian island, divers filmed sandbar sharks cruising over the rocks.
Hiding below some of them was a smaller hunter, the blue runner.
It rides under the shark for about thirty seconds, then bursts out at little fish.
Hunting in a pack, blue runners get spotted over ninety-five percent of the time. From behind a shark, one in ten.
Scientists filmed thirty-four ambushes. The shark is just the disguise.

description:
At Lampione Island in the Mediterranean, blue runners shadow sandbar sharks and dart out to attack smaller fish.
In a 2025 Ecology study of 34 recorded ambushes, prey noticed the shark-hidden attacker only about 10% of the time, versus over 95% for pack attacks.
Would you have guessed a fish uses a shark as camouflage?
first_comment: Riding under the shark may also save the blue runner energy and keep it safe from its own predators. Smart hunter or freeloader?
